mappings.note: What 'काफ़िले' means here (the band of those who die for the country). A diction gloss, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9.
What the songwriter wants to say to his countrymen -- to awaken love of country in them. An expectation placed on the nation, hence C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-4.
What must be done to stop the enemy-Ravan (kill him). A content-level answer from the गीत, so LO-4 rather than LO-5's symbol work.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses (the countrymen). Construing the poem's mode of address, so LO-5; the items that also ask what is expected of them are C-H2.1-LO-9.
Who wrote the song. Authorship identification, hence C-H2.3.
The भाव of life embracing death (= self-sacrifice). A line read for its बलिदान sense, so C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
What the poet advises his साथी -- to tie the कफ़न on their heads. A call placed on the listeners, so C-H2.1-LO-9; the item asking what the idiom means is LO-5.
What the wounded soldier does not grieve over (losing his head). Factual recall, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
The भाव of 'जान देने की रुत' -- the rare chance to die for the country. Line read for its sacrifice, so C-H2.1-LO-10 and not LO-5.
How God is addressed in the text (दयावान). Mapped LO-4 as a text detail, but flagged: no such address occurs in कर चले हम फ़िदा, so this item may be misfiled from another poem -- reported.
What kind of family Kaifi Azmi's was (of artists). कवि-परिचय, so the literature competency rather than a poem outcome.
Which language Kaifi Azmi wrote in originally (Urdu). A fact about the poet, so C-H2.3 and not LO-5.
To whom the soldiers hand over the country (the countrymen). The handover is the expectation C-H2.1-LO-9 names, rather than plain recall under LO-4.
What gladdens the soldiers (they let no stain fall on the country's honour). A fact of the गीत, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
The soldiers' state as they died (full of patriotism and pride). Content recall, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-10.
Meaning of 'राह कुर्बानियों की न वीरान हो' -- those willing to sacrifice must never be few. Line analysis for the उत्तरदायित्व भाव, hence C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
How the soldiers defended the country (by falling in battle). A fact, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What 'सीता का दामन' stands for (the country's soil). Metaphor construal, so LO-5 and not C-H2.1-LO-10.
How the soldiers have inspired the young -- by staying ready to die for the country. What the soldiers ask of the coming generation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-4.
Which hardships the border soldiers face (snowbound heights, struggle, the enemy). Content, so LO-4; the 5-mark item that argues the song is their heart's voice is C-H2.1-LO-10.

What message the song gives -- love of country and readiness to give everything in a crisis. That message is about one's duty to the nation, so C-H2.1-LO-11; the प्रतिपाद्य items, which merely state the poem's burden, are LO-5.
Whose आँचल the land is held as pure as (Sita's). Identifying the comparison, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
What is hardest after freedom is won (keeping it). A reflection on the citizen's continuing duty drawn from the song, so C-H2.1-LO-11 rather than LO-4.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses AND what is expected of them. The second half is the defining C-H2.1-LO-9 deliverable, so that outcome rather than the bare address gloss under LO-5.
The तात्पर्य of drawing a line of blood, and whom 'रावण' is used for. Both halves construe the song's Ramayana imagery, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What message the poet gives us -- to awaken देशभक्ति and readiness to sacrifice in coming generations. A duty-directed message, so C-H2.1-LO-11 and not LO-5.

Which काफ़िला must be kept moving, and why -- the poet's hope that successors keep coming. The 'why' makes it the soldiers' expectation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than the bare gloss of 'काफ़िला' under LO-5.
What 'आज धरती बनी है दुल्हन' says about the earth -- the bridal red read as the blood of the fallen. Metaphor construal, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
To whom the soldiers entrust the वतन. The handover and the charge that goes with it, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-4.
Which रस predominates and why (वीर रस). Naming a रस is कला-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than any content outcome.

Describe the hardships soldiers willingly accept and establish that the song is their heart's voice. The deliverable is the बलिदान और उत्तरदायित्व भाव read out of the lines, so C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-4's fact list.
Make clear the संदेश of 'अब तुम्हारे हवाले वतन साथियो'. A message about the duty now handed to the reader, so C-H2.1-LO-11 rather than LO-5.
The तात्पर्य of drawing a line of blood on the ground. Construing the Lakshman-rekha image, so LO-5, matching the companion item that pairs it with 'रावण'.
What 'जवानी खूं में नहाने' means -- falling in battle for the country. The phrase is read for its sacrifice, hence C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5's imagery items.
What must be done so the road of sacrifice is not deserted -- every citizen must stay ready. A demand on the countrymen, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What 'सांस थमती गई, नब्ज़ जमती गई' means -- fighting to the last breath without bowing. Line analysis for the बलिदान भाव, so C-H2.1-LO-10.
Which two जश्न the poem speaks of. A list drawn from the text, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-11.
Why the earth is called a दुलहन (blood-red bridal dress; the wish that it stay green and rich). Metaphor construal, hence LO-5.
What 'हिमालय का सर' means -- the country's honour. Symbol construal, so LO-5; the item reading the same line as an act of sacrifice is C-H2.1-LO-10.
Why the poet uses the word 'रावण' (for the country's enemies). Figure construal, LO-5 rather than LO-4.
How the poet renders the moment the heroes die. The marks go to the बलिदान भाव carried by those lines, so C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
Why the earth is called a दुल्हन. Metaphor construal, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses and why -- because the soldiers expect the living to keep serving the country. The 'why' carries the expectation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than the address gloss under LO-5.
The soldier's single purpose (to defend the country). A proposition of the गीत, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-11.
Which 'रुत' the poet means -- the season for sacrifice. The phrase is read for its बलिदान sense, hence C-H2.1-LO-10 and not LO-5.
Meaning of 'सिर पर कफ़न बाँधना' as used in the song. The idiom is read inside the text, so LO-5; C-H2.2 would fit only the idiom asked in the abstract.
What 'रावण' symbolises (the foreign enemy). Symbol identification, LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Whom the address 'साथियो' is for (Indians). A bare address gloss with no expectation asked, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9.
What the Himalaya symbolises (Indians' self-respect). Symbol identification, hence LO-5.
What 'सीता' symbolises (Bharat Mata). Symbol identification, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
What the soldiers hope for from their countrymen / what they expect of them. This is the textbook case of C-H2.1-LO-9, not LO-4.
Why the earth is called a दुल्हन, here answered through the wish that the land stay adorned and fertile. Metaphor construal, so LO-5.
The song's historical background (the 1962 India-China war). Contextual fact about the text, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-4.
Whom the poet calls Ram and Lakshman, and why. Construing the poem's analogy, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9, since the question is about the figure rather than the demand.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses and which काफ़िला must be carried forward. The second half is the expectation laid on countrymen, hence C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-5.
The प्रतिपाद्य of the poem in about 100 words. A statement of the song's central burden, so LO-5 -- C-H2.1-LO-11 is kept for items that ask the student to respond about their own duty.
Which death the poem calls good and why, and what संदेश follows. The deliverable ends in the duty it lays on the reader, so C-H2.1-LO-11 rather than LO-5's theme statement.

Two halves: the background the song was written against (contextual, C-H2.3) and its प्रतिपाद्य in the student's own words (LO-5). Both carry marks, so both are cited. Its model answer dates the war to 1967 -- reported as a factual defect.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses and which काफ़िला is to be carried on. Duplicate of the earlier paired item and mapped C-H2.1-LO-9 the same way, not LO-5.

Two deliverables: what the soldiers expect of their countrymen (C-H2.1-LO-9) and whether we are meeting those expectations, argued (C-H2.1-LO-11 -- the student's own reasoned response on duty). Its stem carries a wrapped option list and its answer belongs to a different MCQ; reported.
